issues.title: [Bug]: `check` in a class field initializer compiles when init can't return an error, then `new` crashes with a Go interface-conversion error
issues.output:
error: interface conversion: values.BalValue is *values.Error, not *values.Object
        at main(r1500.bal:20)
issues.reasoning: Reproduces on main. A clean-context spec review agreed: init() returns nil (explicit in A, implicit for B per §6.8.1.5), so per §6.8.2 `new` has static type A/B and the check-fail from the field initializer has nowhere legal to go (§6.2: a normally completed result must belong to the static type). The front end should reject the `check` (or the `new`). Instead it compiles, the error value is stored in `a`, and reading a field crashes with a Go type assertion. The root cause is the missing front-end check. Not frontend-crash: compilation succeeds and the crash is at runtime. Related to #1219 (check in parameter/record field defaults), not a duplicate.

issues.title: [Bug]: conditional expression is never treated as an isolated expression (rejected when returned from a lock in an isolated class)
issues.output:
error[SEMANTIC_ERROR]: not an isolated expression
  --> r1501.bal:14:20
issues.reasoning: Reproduces on main. §6.2.6: a conditional-expr or list-constructor-expr is isolated if all its subexpressions are isolated, and readonly-typed expressions are isolated. Here the condition is boolean and the branch members are int, so the return expression is isolated and §7.23 is satisfied. Expected output is [] then [4]. The front end wrongly rejects a valid program. Related to #1429 (same diagnostic for a different construct), not a duplicate.

issues.title: [Bug]: resource methods whose paths diverge at a non-singleton segment are not rejected
issues.reasoning: Reproduces on main. §5.6.3.5: ["users", int] vs ["users", string], and ["items", int] vs ["items", int...], diverge at position 2 without a singleton string member there, so each pair is a compile-time error. The front end is missing this check. No duplicate found.

issues.title: [Bug]: including a `service`/`client` object type with `*T` is accepted without the matching qualifier
issues.reasoning: Reproduces on main. §5.6.3.8: if a referenced object type or class has an isolated, service or client qualifier Q, the referencing object type descriptor must also have Q. `type Plain object { *Cl; }` is definitely an error. `class Impl { *Svc; }` is very likely an error too (a class describes an object type, §8.6, and the isolated equivalent is already enforced for classes). The runtime result `i is Svc == false` is consistent with Impl not being a service object, so the bug is the missing front-end diagnostic. No duplicate found.
